'''Rosmarie Honegger''' (born 1947) is a Swiss [[Lichenology|lichenologist]] and Emeritus Professor at the [[University of Zurich]]. 

==Academic career==

Honegger was born in 1947 and grew up in [[Emmental (valley)|Emmental]], Switzerland.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The Rhynie Chert – our earliest terrestrial ecosystem revisited|url=https://royalsociety.org/science-events-and-lectures/2017/03/rhynie-chert/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-03|website=Royal Society|language=en-gb}}</ref> She developed an early interest in plants, and was recommended to study [[lichen]]s by a biology teacher. This led to a research project involving compiling a [[flora]] of her home town, which, in 1967, led to her earning a prize at an international [[science fair]] in [[San Francisco]]. The same year, she began studies at the [[University of Basel]].<ref name="Kärnefelt 2009"/>

Honegger earned her PhD in biology from the University of Basel in 1976. Her doctoral research examined the structure and function of the [[ascus]] (the [[spore]]-bearing structure) in the lichen genus ''[[Lecanora]]'', using microscopic techniques.<ref name="Kärnefelt 2009"/> In 1977 she accepted a [[postdoctoral research]] position in the Institute of Plant Biology at the University of Zurich. After a time working at the [[University of California, Riverside]] she returned to Switzerland as professor in the Institute of Plant Biology of the University of Zurich.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Stofer|first=Silvia|date=2008-07-18|title=Acharius Medallists: Rosmarie Honegger|url=http://www.lichenology.org/Awards/Acharius_Honegger.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-03|website=International Association for Lichenology}}</ref> Honegger retired in 2009<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Rosmarie Honegger|url=https://bio-protocol.org/UserHome.aspx?id=1006084|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-03|website=BIO-PROTOCOL}}</ref> as Emeritus Professor.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Prof. Rosmarie Honegger|url=https://www.botinst.uzh.ch/en/research/emeriti/rhonegger.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-03|website=University of Zurich|language=en}}</ref> From 2011 she worked with [[Dianne Edwards]], a [[palaeobotanist]] at the [[Cardiff University]] on lichen fossils found on the Welsh borderland.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite Q|Q34913287}}</ref><ref>{{Cite Q|Q47818255}}</ref>

Honegger was awarded the [[International Association for Lichenology]]'s [[Acharius Medal]] for her lifetime work in lichenology in 2008<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Acharius Medallists|url=http://www.lichenology.org/index.html?/Awards/AchariusMedallists.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-03|website=International Association for Lichenology}}</ref> and in 2015 she received the [[Linnean Medal]] recognising her contribution to the natural sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2015-06-15|title=Medal Winners|url=https://www.linnean.org/news/2015/06/15/15th-june-2015-medal-winners|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-03|website=The Linnean Society|language=en-GB}}</ref> She was one of the "Fifty influential lichenologists" discussed in [[Ingvar Kärnefelt]]'s 2011 review of the scientific progress of lichenology and the scientists who study it.<ref name="Kärnefelt 2009"/>

{{botanist|Honegger|inline=yes}}

Among the lichens named in her honour is ''[[Xanthomendoza rosmarieae]]'', described in 2011 by [[Sergey Kondratyuk]] and Kärnefelt.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Names Record: Xanthomendoza rosmarieae S.Y. Kondr. & Kärnefelt, in Lumbsch et al., Phytotaxa 18: 114 (2011)|url=http://www.indexfungorum.org/Names/NamesRecord.asp?RecordID=517818|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-03|website=Index Fungorum}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Xanthomendoza rosmarieae|url=https://www.mycobank.org/page/Name%20details%20page/name/Xanthomendoza|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-02-03|website=Mycobank Database}}</ref>
